item.description:
What's new in 2.40.0

A big one, and most of it in Shepherd: a panel that shows what each agent can reach and lets you give it more, a key display for recording demos, an undo for closing an agent, and paths and links in a pane that resolve properly on a server instead of only on this Mac. The image editor every tool shares has been rebuilt, and can take the background out.

MCP servers, per agent

  • ⇧⌘M shows what the agent in this pane can reach — its MCP servers, read from the agent's own configuration.
  • Add one from a catalog rather than by editing a file: pick a server, and it is installed for that agent on that machine, server or this Mac.
  • Every server wears its own logo, on a ground it can be seen on, and signing in happens in the panel rather than somewhere else.

Show the keys you press — ⌥⌘K

  • For recording a demo. Hold a chord and it appears on screen as keycaps, captioned with what it did in the same words the ⌘/ card uses.
  • Chords only, and that is a safety property — nothing without ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ is ever drawn, so a prompt, a path or a password typed into a pane cannot reach the video.
  • Drag the pill to place it in a picture of the window it will be in, with nine snap targets; dropping it shows you the real thing, full size, where it will actually sit.
  • Holding the dictation key shows a red dot and names the agent the words will land in — the one part of a recording a viewer cannot otherwise work out.

Reopen the agent you just closed — ⇧⌘W

  • ⌘W closes an agent; ⇧⌘W brings it back, in the same conversation, with its own name and folder and the permissions flag it was started with.
  • Closing a tab or a project counts too — ⇧⌘W walks back through them one at a time, rebuilding the tab or reopening the folder if it has to.
  • Twenty deep, kept for a fortnight, and remembered across quitting Dax: closing the wrong agent on Friday and wanting it on Monday is the same mistake.

Paths and links in a pane, on a server

  • A ~ now expands against the machine the path is on. Every tilde path an agent printed on a server used to be resolved against your Mac's home and looked for on the server, where it has never been — so those links never even lit up.
  • A file outside the project is found. Resolution climbs to the root cheaply, and when that misses it searches — the git root first and deepest, then wider and shallower, then the places a server keeps work. Several answers get a picker rather than a guess.
  • One search teaches the pane where it is standing, so the next path resolves instantly.
  • A link wrapped across lines opens whole on a server too. Whether a row had run out of room was measured against this window's width, which is only the wrap width when the pane belongs to this Mac — so multi-row links simply did not work on a remote pane.
  • ⌘-clicking a file on a server downloads it and previews it here.

The image editor, rebuilt

  • A markup bar in groups — tools, size, colour, done — instead of eleven controls in one row.
  • Remove Background, on the bar. Press it again and the background comes back, with everything you have drawn still where you drew it.
  • Rounded corners, by however much you say — a slider, on by default at 1.5%, remembered for the next picture.
  • One colour well that opens the whole palette, and 1–7 still pick a colour directly.

Opening a folder

  • A folder already open is switched to, not opened again. ⌘O, the server's browser, the Recent menu, the home screen's list, ⌘J's folder rows and a folder dropped on the window all used to make a second project rooted at the same path with an empty terminal in it.
  • It lands on an agent's pane rather than a spare shell, and answering "which agent?" now puts the keyboard in the pane.
  • ⇧⌘N clones a repo — paste a URL and it lands in your projects folder and opens.

Around the window

  • ⌘/ is five tabs rather than one very tall column, and the empty screen says Show Keyboard Shortcuts where you would look for it.
  • Both machine switchers put This Mac first and order servers by how recently you connected, and neither counts sleeping agents.
  • Closing an agent shows a door on the way out rather than a skull, and tab chips have a close button.
  • Agent Watch sorts into three lists and draws the herd as sheep, and can watch the agents on a server.

Selecting, copying and links

  • A selection is copied when the mouse comes up, rather than needing a second deliberate step for something you have already finished doing.
  • Dragging past the edge scrolls the pane, so a selection can run past what is on screen instead of stopping at it.
  • Copy carries its formatting where that helps — and the plain copy loses the table borders, which were never text you wanted in your paste.
  • Hovering a link says ⌘-click, and it lights in its own pane's colour, all of it rather than part.

New Project

  • The project appears the moment herdr says it exists, rather than after the sheet has finished everything else.
  • The sheet waits for the work it started, and says which part is taking the time.
  • Cancel actually calls it off — it used to half-end a create it could not stop.

Also in this release

  • A command that has just been handed a secret runs sandboxed, and a pasted instruction can no longer teach an agent to print one.
  • A second Shepherd window runs its own herdr session, instead of the two fighting over one.
  • You can reach an agent on this Mac while Shepherd is showing a server.
  • A pane can arrive without a working directory instead of refusing to arrive.
  • A server connection test says three words where it used to say seventy-five lines.
  • Signed, notarized, universal (Apple Silicon & Intel), macOS 14+.
